marrow__ANAT_CH19_Q015.takeaway: Pacchionian bodies are arachnoid granulations that protrude through dura into venous sinuses.
marrow__ANAT_CH19_Q015.displayText:
Pacchionian bodies (arachnoid granulations) are focal pouches of arachnoid mater and subarachnoid space protruding through the walls of dural venous sinuses.

Option B: Tuft of capillaries enclosed by pia mater lined by ependymal cells forms tela choroidea. It secretes CSF.

Option C: Calcareous deposits in the astrocytes of the pineal gland are known as brain sand or corpora arenacea.

Option D: Shrunken, yellow-brown, cystic lesions in the gyri and subarachnoid space associated with head injury are called plaque jaune.

rationales.b: Tela choroidea is the vascular pia-derived tissue that supports the choroid plexus, not an arachnoid granulation.
rationales.c: Pineal calcifications are corpora arenacea (brain sand), not Pacchionian bodies.
rationales.d: Plaque jaune refers to shrunken yellow-brown cystic lesions after head injury; it is not an arachnoid granulation.

marrow__ANAT_CH19_Q016.takeaway: The choroid plexus produces most CSF; ependymal and perivascular routes contribute less.
marrow__ANAT_CH19_Q016.displayText:
The case suggests CSF rhinorrhea and the image shows the double-ring sign. CSF mainly forms in the choroid plexus. It is absorbed back by the arachnoid villi.

Formation of CSF:
• Major contributor - Choroid plexuses
• Minor contributors - Ependymal cells lining the ventricles, brain substance through the perivascular spaces

CSF is produced at a rate of 550 ml/day. The normal adult volume of CSF is 150 ml, and it is cycled about 3.7 times a day. The normal CSF pressure is 70-180 mm H2O.

rationales.a: Ventricular ependymocytes contribute a smaller share; the choroid plexus is the major CSF source.
rationales.c: Perivascular spaces are a minor source of CSF, not the majority contributor.
rationales.d: Microglia are CNS immune cells and do not produce most CSF.

marrow__ANAT_CH19_Q017.takeaway: The source answer key selects adenohypophysis as not a circumventricular organ; this classification and the stated BBB rationale require subject review.
marrow__ANAT_CH19_Q017.displayText:
Circumventricular organs are those structures in the brain that are devoid of the blood-brain barrier. Adenohypophysis is not devoid of a blood-brain barrier (BBB).

Neurohypophysis is devoid of the blood-brain barrier.

rationales.a: OVLT is a conventional circumventricular organ with specialized fenestrated vasculature.
rationales.b: Median eminence is a conventional circumventricular organ associated with the hypothalamic–pituitary portal system.
rationales.d: Pineal gland is a conventional circumventricular organ; the printed key selects adenohypophysis as the exception, but source rationale requires medical review.

reconstruction.reconstructedContent:
Circumventricular organs are those structures in the brain that are devoid of the blood-brain barrier. Adenohypophysis is not devoid of a blood-brain barrier (BBB).

Neurohypophysis is devoid of the blood-brain barrier. The source-keyed answer is retained for this candidate, but whether adenohypophysis should be included among circumventricular organs and its BBB description require a medical subject review.
evidenceBasis: Anatomy ED8 source explanation, question 17, page 360; answer key retained unchanged.

NCBI Endotext, Functional Anatomy of the Hypothalamus and Pituitary: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279126/ lists conventional circumventricular organs, including median eminence and pineal, but not adenohypophysis.
A definitive guide to the blood-brain barrier (PMCID: PMC6692757): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6692757/ distinguishes the neurohypophysis and median eminence in the classic CVO group.

Development and Function of the Blood-Brain Barrier in the Context of Metabolic Control (PMCID: PMC5399017): https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5399017/ includes “pituitary” among seven CVO categories.
reconstruction.reviewNote: Do not teach the source’s categorical claim that adenohypophysis is BBB-protected as settled without subject review. Keep the source key but flag classification ambiguity; do not alter or remove the source completeness gate.
